title: Delineate anything flow: fast, country-level field boundary detection from any source
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate satellite data-based field boundary delineation is essential for land management and agricultural statistics, but integrating tile-level predictions into continuous large-area vector products introduces topological errors and computational challenges. We present Delineate Anything Flow (DelAnyFlow), a framework for scalable field instance mapping that integrates the YOLOv11-based DelAny model with structured post-processing, cross-tile instance unification, vectorization, and topology-consistent simplification. DelAny is trained on the Field Boundary Instance Segmentation-22 M (FBIS-22M) dataset, containing 672,909 multi-resolution patches from 0.25 to 10 m and 22.9 million field instances. It achieves the mean average precision with the intersection over union (IoU) threshold set at 0.5 (mAP@0.5) of 0.720 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.477, while providing substantially faster inference than the zero-shot segment anything model (SAM2). Component-level evaluation shows that cross-tile unification reduces seam-induced field fragmentation by a factor of 4–6, while anchor-guided simplification reduces separated neighbouring fields from about 20% to 0.2% at comparable geometric compression. Demonstrating operational scalability, DelAnyFlow mapped Ukraine’s entire 603,000 km2 territory in 5.4 h on a single workstation. Quantitative comparisons with independent operational products show larger IoU values and small-object recall (producer accuracy), particularly for fragmented agricultural landscapes; DelAnyFlow reaches an IoU of 0.971 and a small-object recall of 0.878, compared with 0.926 and 0.405 for the best operational product. The framework therefore provides a reproducible pathway from tile-level GeoAI predictions to spatially continuous, topologically consistent field-boundary products at regional and national scales. Code, models, the dataset, and national vectors are available at https://lavreniuk.github.io/Delineate-Anything/ .

title: A Cascaded Framework with a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN Model for Pre- and Post-Treatment Glioma Segmentation
abstract: Accurate glioma segmentation is vital for diagnosis and follow-up, but manual segmentation is time-consuming, subjective, and variable across interpreters. Gliomas are heterogeneous in size, shape, and location. Deep learning has therefore emerged as a potential solution. CNNs excel at local features but may struggle with long-range dependencies, whereas Vision Transformers capture global context efficiently but incur higher computational complexity. Most previous studies focused on pre-treatment gliomas; post-treatment cases with resection cavities (RCs) remain less explored. This study proposes a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN (CMC-Seg) model within a cascaded framework for pre- and post-treatment diffuse glioma segmentation, aiming to balance accuracy and computational cost. Experiments used BraTS 2025 mpMRI of diffuse glioma patients. After preprocessing, a coarse segmentation model extracted tumor-centered patches, which were fed to CMC-Seg for fine-grained segmentation. CMC-Seg was compared with 3D U-Net, SegResNet, SwinUNETR, UNETR, nnFormer, and SegMamba. On the test set, CMC-Seg achieved the highest mean Dice (81.20%) and non-enhancing tumor core (NETC) Dice (77.09%). It also achieved an RC Dice of 78.63% and the lowest 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95; 4.39 mm). Results were comparable to CNN and Mamba baselines and significantly better than Transformer-based baselines (P < 0.05). CMC-Seg required the fewest inference GFLOPs (381.49). Ablation experiments indicated that multi-direction scanning and cross-attention improved performance, particularly for RC (P < 0.05). Grad-CAM explainability experiments showed that CMC-Seg focuses on diagnostically relevant tumor regions.

title: DREAM: Dual-Memory Reasoning for Anticipatory 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving
abstract: Autonomous driving systems must not only interpret the current scene but also anticipate perceptual challenges such as occlusions, sparse observations, and recurring failure patterns. However, most existing LiDAR semantic segmentation methods operate in a frame-centric manner, processing each scan independently and discarding past contextual experience, which limits robustness under dynamic scene changes. We propose DREAM, a Dual-memory REAsoning framework for continual LiDAR seMantic segmentation that reframes perception as an experience-driven and anticipatory process. DREAM maintains two complementary memory banks in a strictly online setting: a latent memory that stores compact semantic abstractions of previously observed scenes, and an error memory that records representations associated with uncertain predictions. At each timestep, relevant memory entries are retrieved via cosine similarity and integrated into the feature space through a lightweight modulation mechanism, enabling the model to reinforce consistent semantic patterns while suppressing recurring failure modes. The backbone remains frozen and no past scans are replayed, ensuring computational efficiency and bounded memory growth. Extensive experiments on multiple large-scale LiDAR benchmarks demonstrate that DREAM achieves state-of-the-art performance, with consistent improvements on dynamic and small-scale objects, highlighting the effectiveness of persistent and error-aware memory for robust long-horizon perception.

title: Lightweight Spectral Subspace Filtering for Trojan-Resilient AI Inference Engines
abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a significant security threat to deep neural networks (DNNs) deployed on AI inference engines and hardware accelerators. By embedding hidden triggers during training, these attacks induce malicious behavior while maintaining high accuracy on benign inputs. Multi-trigger backdoor attacks are particularly challenging to detect and mitigate because of the distributed and stealthy nature of their effects. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a training-free Spectral Subspace Filtering framework that detects and suppresses backdoor-induced activations by analyzing latent feature representations. Exploiting the geometric separation between benign and malicious feature distributions, the framework employs Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to identify the dominant malicious subspace and performs inference-time spectral scrubbing through activation projection. This approach suppresses backdoor effects without model retraining, requiring only a small set of triggered samples collected offline. Experimental evaluation across CNN and transformer architectures, including AlexNet, ResNet18, VGG16, MobileNetV2, and Vision Transformer (ViT), demonstrates that the proposed method reduces the attack success rate (ASR) from 94.2-99.8% to an average of 2.07%, while preserving clean accuracy of up to 98.54% with low inference overhead. The framework also demonstrates robustness across varying poisoning rates and multiple concurrent triggers, highlighting its potential as a lightweight runtime defense for enhancing the security and reliability of AI inference engines against backdoor attacks.

title: DeclareViT: Decoupling Early Classification from Feature Refinement with Exit Query for Efficient ViTs
abstract: Vision Transformers achieve remarkable recognition performance but incur substantial computational cost during inference, limiting their use in latency- and compute-constrained deployment scenarios. Early-exit inference offers a promising solution by allowing easy samples to terminate at intermediate layers. However, existing approaches typically couple early classification with the shared backbone, requiring intermediate representations to support both early classification and subsequent feature refinement. Under joint training, the corresponding optimization objectives jointly update shared backbone parameters, which can lead to conflicting gradient directions. Motivated by this observation, we introduce DeclareViT, a framework that decouples early classification from feature refinement. Each exit uses a dedicated query to read intermediate features through one-way cross-attention without modifying the backbone token stream. The query branches are optimized for early classification while the backbone and final classifier remain frozen. Across ViT, DeiT, and Swin on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, and Food-101, DeclareViT consistently establishes a state-of-the-art accuracy-efficiency trade-off: It achieves 1.58 times to 2.57 times multiply-accumulate (MAC)-based speed-up with only a 0.39-1.91 percentage-point accuracy drop. Wall-clock measurements on CPU and GPU further demonstrate practical inference acceleration. Code is available at https://github.com/TUDa-HWAI/DeclareViT.

title: BQDNA: Multi-Head Binary Spherical Quantization for Genomic Sequence Modeling
abstract: Decoding biological information from long, repetitive DNA remains challenging. Genomic language models (gLMs) often follow the conventional language-model pretrain-and-adapt paradigm. However, the lack of inherent semantic segmentation and prior rules makes hand-crafted tokenizers like k-mer and BPE suboptimal. We introduce context-aware \textbf{BQVAE} for scalar quantization of DNA and \textbf{BQDNA}, an autoregressive gLM supporting multi-head codebooks. Comprehensive experiments reveal that: (1) unique training dynamics of vector quantization in DNA space, including the importance of alignment between training corpus and downstream data. (2) superior performance of BQVAE over hand-crafted tokenizers and vanilla VQVAE. (3) remarkable cross-species generalization capability of BQDNA, which achieves state-of-the-art performance with merely 0.1B multi-species training for BQVAE and 1 epoch training on hg38 for BQDNA, outperforming gLMs pretrained with 10$\sim$100x more tokens. Our findings underscore the potential of learned vector quantization for genomic sequence representation. Code is available at https://github.com/Sophie10001b/BQDNA

title: SpectralGS: Spectral Gaussian Splatting for Unsupervised Spectral Super-Resolution
abstract: Unsupervised spectral super-resolution aims to recover spectral information from RGB images without paired hyperspectral data. However, the limited spectral information in RGB observations makes learning an effective spatial-spectral representation challenging, requiring the incorporation of structured spectral modeling with sensor imaging. In this paper, we propose SpectralGS, a spectral Gaussian splatting framework comprising two components: Shared Spectral Gaussian Representation and Spectral Response Projection Rendering. The representation module constructs a continuous spatial-spectral representation via shared spectral and local spatial Gaussian primitives, exploiting the low-rank spectral structure of hyperspectral images. The rendering module utilizes the spectral response function (SRF) to apply integral projection to the continuous representation, blending it to generate an RGB image. Consistency between the rendered and observed RGB images provides training supervision. Our main contribution is a Gaussian splatting framework that integrates structured continuous spatial-spectral representation with imaging response-based rendering, enabling unsupervised spectral reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

title: Why Adaptive Optimizers Struggle with Large Convolution Kernels
abstract: Large convolution kernels enlarge the receptive fields of ConvNets at a modest computational cost, but they are notoriously difficult to train. Existing large-kernel networks therefore rely on costly training techniques, such as parallel small-kernel branches with batch normalization. In this paper, we trace this difficulty to adaptive optimizers such as Adam, which normalize the update of every weight separately. Since input features rarely average to zero, all weights of a kernel share a common gradient, and these optimizers move the mean of a $k\times k$ kernel $k$ times as far as a single parameter. We find this mean amplification in widely used ConvNets and vision transformers, and show that it can force the maximal learning rate to fall as $1/k^2$. We further prove that the basis of the discrete cosine transform (DCT) isolates the mean and is the only orthonormal basis that diagonalizes every stationary gradient statistic with mirrored boundaries. We therefore train large kernels through their DCT coefficients and convert them back after training. The resulting method, DCT-Rep, requires only a few lines of code and adds no parameters, no inference cost and negligible training overhead. Extensive experiments on image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation and image restoration show that DCT-Rep consistently improves large-kernel ConvNets and vision transformers, by $+0.79\%$ top-1 accuracy for a large-kernel ConvNeXt-T and $+0.43\%$ for ViT-S/16 on ImageNet-1K, $+1.4$ box AP on COCO, $+1.2$ mIoU on ADE20K and up to $+0.4$ dB on image deblurring, where the gain grows with the kernel size.

title: loopxDINO: Dense Visual Prediction via Iterative Latent Reasoning
abstract: Standard dense visual prediction architectures scale representation capacity by stacking deep feedforward decoders (6-16 transformer layers with 50M-200M parameters). This explicit layer stacking brings substantial activation memory overhead during backpropagation, requires high off-chip memory bandwidth for non-tied weights, and uses static computational allocation that cannot adapt to spatial image complexity. We propose loopxDINO, which replaces physical decoder depth with iterative latent reasoning. It has two decoupled components: (1) a frozen DINOv2-Base backbone extracting spatial features in one forward pass and caching static Key-Value representations in GPU memory; (2) a compact weight-tied Looped Cross-Attention Decoder (7.96M core, 14.85M total trainable parameters) that recurrently updates queries across T iterations. Recurrence is stabilized by step-conditioned adaLN, LayerNorm-based hyper-ellipsoid manifold regularization, and learnable residual contraction damping. Intermediate mask predictions are fed back as spatial attention biases to guide queries toward ambiguous contours with no extra parameters. On Pascal VOC 2012 semantic segmentation with a single RTX 5060 Ti 16GB GPU, loopxDINO (T=2) achieves 85.66% mIoU and 65.01% Boundary IoU. It outperforms 6-layer DINO-Trans6L (54.06M params) by +1.09% mIoU and +7.41% Boundary IoU with 72.5% fewer parameters. Compared to 4-layer DINO-FCN4L probe (2.43M params, 83.82% mIoU), loopxDINO improves boundary delineation by +6.43% bIoU and occlusion resilience by +6.76% mIoU (60% patch masking). With Adaptive Computation Time (ACT), it reaches 87.3 FPS and retains 29.64% mIoU under 60% occlusion (+5.83% over DINO-Trans6L). Source code, pre-trained weights and evaluation suites are open-sourced under Apache 2.0 at https://github.com/loopxDINO/loopxDINO

title: Monte Carlo biphasic estimation of fire properties (McBEF): Part I, algorithm formulation
abstract: Sub-pixel fire characterization is essential for quantifying wildfire energetics, combustion phase dynamics, and their atmospheric impacts from satellite observations. This study presents a series of Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) to systematically evaluate the influence of temperature phase complexity, channel selection, and intra-phase temperature heterogeneity on the performance of a Bayesian retrieval framework. Using synthetic observations derived from a multi-phase radiance model, we assess retrieval skill across key fire properties—including Fire Radiative Power (FRP), visible energy fraction (VEF), and flaming heat flux—under realistic sensor constraints. Results show that a bi-phasic fire model provides a strong balance between accuracy and observational feasibility, outperforming conventional approaches such as Wooster’s FRP regression, particularly in low-intensity fire scenarios. FRP is the retrieved quantity most resilient to model and observational uncertainties, while VEF and heat flux estimates are more sensitive to both fire phase partitioning and spectral coverage. Shortwave and mid-infrared bands, especially the day–night band (DNB) and 2.25 μ m channels, are shown to offer the greatest constraint on retrieval accuracy. We further analyze the impact of intra-phase temperature variability and propose practical filtering strategies for identifying low-confidence cases, such as smoldering-dominated fires. The theoretical framework is applicable to multi-channel fire observations more generally, while its companion Part II implementation focuses specifically on nighttime VIIRS observations.

title: Multi-angular remote sensing-derived directional fractional vegetation cover for improved C-factor estimation in RUSLE modeling
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The cover and management factor ( C -factor) is a crucial parameter influencing the accuracy of soil erosion model estimates. However, conventional approaches often overlook the influence of vegetation vertical structure, particularly understory vegetation, which may lead to biased estimation of erosion severity. To address this issue, a synergistic C -factor estimation framework was developed that integrates multi-angular remote sensing (RS) observations and directional fractional vegetation cover ( DFVC ) to enhance the characterization of vegetation structure and improve C -factor estimation accuracy. The PROSAIL model was used to simulate canopy reflectance under different viewing angles, from which a dataset of multi-angular vegetation indices (VIs) was constructed. Among these VIs, the index most strongly correlated with leaf area index ( LAI ) was selected to develop a progressive “VIs– LAI – DFVC – C -factor” estimation model. The applicability of the method was further evaluated using field measurements collected across different vegetation types and structural conditions. The perpendicular vegetation index ( PVI ) was found to be significantly correlated with LAI and was identified as the optimal feature for LAI retrieval. Among the multi-angular combinations, the three-angle combination of 0°, 36°, and 55° was retained for LAI retrieval and achieved an RMSE of 0.233 and a MAPE of 0.059. Based on the overall evaluation, the 0° + 36° configuration was adopted for final DFVC -based C -factor mapping. The proposed estimation framework demonstrated high reliability ( R 2 = 0.754), with a mean C -factor estimate value of 0.019 in the study area. This study highlights the importance of incorporating vegetation vertical structure information in C -factor estimation and demonstrates that multi-angular RS can offer effective complementary information for characterizing structural features such as canopy gaps and directional occlusion. The proposed framework presents a new approach for quantitative soil erosion monitoring and environmental management.

title: Sound2Vision: Generating Diverse Visuals from Audio through Cross-Modal Latent Alignment
abstract: How does audio describe the world around us? In this work, we propose a method for generating images of visual scenes from diverse in-the-wild sounds. This cross-modal generation task is challenging due to the significant information gap between auditory and visual signals. We address this challenge by designing a model that aligns audio-visual modalities by enriching audio features with visual information and translating them into the visual latent space. These features are then fed into the pre-trained image generator to produce images. To enhance image quality, we use sound source localization to select audio-visual pairs with strong cross-modal correlations. Our method achieves substantially better results on the VEGAS and VGGSound datasets compared to previous work and demonstrates control over the generation process through simple manipulations to the input waveform or latent space. Furthermore, we analyze the geometric properties of the learned embedding space and demonstrate that our learning approach effectively aligns audio-visual signals for cross-modal generation. Based on this analysis, we show that our method is agnostic to specific design choices, showing its generalizability by integrating various model architectures and different types of audio-visual data.

title: Recurrent Point Transformer via Test-Time Training
abstract: Real-world point clouds are not naturally bounded: 3D scans grow as sensors move through rooms, LiDAR surveys extend across forest plots, and 4D captures can span thousands of frames. Yet most point-cloud encoders are designed for fixed-size inputs, forcing inference-time cropping or tiling that loses long-range context and requires ad-hoc output stitching. We formulate arbitrary-extent point-cloud segmentation as recurrent sequence-of-chunks processing and introduce PoinTTT, a recurrent point-cloud encoder built on Point Transformer V3 (PTv3). PoinTTT augments PTv3 with residual Large Chunk Test-Time Training (LaCT) layers in both the encoder and decoder. Each LaCT layer maintains compact fast weights as recurrent state: tokens from each chunk update the fast weights, which are then applied to produce chunk features and passed to the next chunk. This design allows PoinTTT to train on fixed-size chunks while processing scenes of arbitrary spatial or temporal extent, with activation memory bounded by the chunk size. A pilot study on ScanNet and nuScenes shows that recurrent TTT improves segmentation over PTv3 baselines. On FOR-instanceV2, PoinTTT achieves state-of-the-art forest semantic segmentation of 87.9 mIoU with nearly constant memory. On HOI4D, online full-sequence recurrent inference carries state across clips rather than resetting at benchmark boundaries, reaching 42.6 mIoU; a matched full-sequence Mamba control reaches approximately 39.9. These results suggest that test-time training is a practical primitive for scalable spatial and temporal point-cloud understanding.

title: What the Background Hides: Thresholds, Vocabularies and Collisions in Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
abstract: Training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) built on CLIP has advanced rapidly, with methods typically ranked by mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) across standard benchmarks. On datasets with a background class, however, implementations rely on per-dataset thresholds and background word lists that are rarely documented or unified (11 of 13 surveyed methods configure per-dataset background decisions). We audit configurations and papers of 13 training-free OVSS methods, re-run seven from official codebases, and compare official settings against a strict unified protocol under pre-registered contracts. The protocol gap depends strongly on the benchmark---ranging from 22.8 mIoU points on PASCAL VOC (VOC21) to 0.1 points (indistinguishable from zero) on ADE20K---and alters pairwise method rankings. Despite large shifts in absolute mIoU, most of the reported improvement of later CLIP-only methods over SCLIP remains under the unified protocol (roughly 79% of the published gain). Decomposing official background handling shows that it combines numeric settings and class-name files whose dominant component reverses across benchmarks, while no tested tuning-free rule transfers reliably across all datasets. Moreover, exact collisions between background words and target names---present in six of seven official COCO-Object configurations through "bed"---make affected classes unpredictable under official post-processing, while the main per-class drops under language-model-generated vocabularies on VOC21 are largely attributable to a few generated terms. We offer reporting recommendations and release our evaluation code, frozen configurations, contracts, and a collision-check tool.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Task-Aware Transformer for Video Procedure Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Procedure learning aims to jointly recognize and localize key steps from instructional videos given an ordered step list. The goal is to predict precise temporal spans for each step. Existing methods typically treat this as a sequence-to-sequence alignment task. However, as the provided step lists lack deeper task-level knowledge, we observe that these models often struggle with two challenges: (1) Missing cross-route task generalization, where models overfit to single annotated pattern and fail to capture the diverse yet semantically valid routes of the same task; and (2) Insufficient temporal-visual grounding, where the absence of concrete timing and appearance priors in the provided step lists leads to boundary drift and step error when predicting on individual videos. To address these challenges, we propose the Task-Aware Transformer (TAT), a unified framework that integrates task-level priors into the alignment process. TAT consists of two complementary components: (i) Task-Aware Structured Memory Construction, which aggregates semantic, temporal, and visual knowledge from multiple execution routes into a structured memory. To ensure the memory remains faithful to supervision, we introduce a Memory Constraint Loss that jointly encodes semantic consistency and temporal order. (ii) Retrieval-Augmented Video-Step Alignment, which retrieves a knowledge-enriched route from the memory to serve as contextual guidance, injecting fine-grained priors into the frame-to-step alignment. We further design two alignment strategies, a lightweight cross-modal decoder and a Vision-Language Model association, to balance efficiency and generalization. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks (YouCookII, COIN, CrossTask, and ProceL) demonstrate that TAT consistently outperforms existing methods, particularly in generalizing to novel procedural compositions, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Learning Physical Priors Embedded in Underwater Imaging and Light Attenuation for Self-Supervised Underwater Depth Estimation
abstract: Depth information is crucial for the perception and navigation of underwater robots. While existing methods incorporate underwater physical priors into self-supervised monocular depth estimation to mitigate the impact of image degradation, challenges such as depth misestimation in background regions, loss of edge details, and limited generalization capabilities remain to be addressed. In this paper, we propose UIEMono, which transforms the physical characteristics of underwater imaging and light propagation into depth estimation cues and incorporates them into the self-supervised learning pipeline. Specifically, multiple networks predict the latent components of the underwater image formation model to reconstruct the input image. This reconstruction process, combined with the geometric projection relationships between adjacent frames, assists the network in learning to infer scene depth. During training, we adopt two distinct estimation strategies for the forward attenuation coefficient: in the early stages, it is predicted as a global constant within each image to ensure training stability; in the later stages, a two-term exponential model is utilized to model its dependency on depth, thereby achieving joint optimization. The constraint relationship between the latent components of homologous images is used to provide additional supervision. We leverage the inherent relationship between depth and light attenuation to provide additional cues for guiding network learning. Furthermore, we weight the reprojection loss based on the intensity differences between channels to avoid the negative impact of photometric errors in background regions. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance and can generalize to a wider range of underwater scenarios.

title: DC-SQEM: Medial Mesh Extraction by Dual Contouring with Spherical Quadric Error Metric
abstract: The medial axis , as a compact representation, describes not only the boundary but also the interior of the shape, and has been widely used in analyzing and simplifying shapes. However, approximating feature-preserving medial axis from unstructured data, such as oriented point clouds, remains challenging due to the lack of explicit connectivity and the presence of noise in the source. We propose DC-SQEM, a dual-contouring-based framework that computes medial meshes (an explicit representation of the medial axis) directly from oriented point clouds without relying on watertight manifold surfaces or volumetric structures. With the help of an adaptive octree, our method fits local medial spheres for each cell based on the Spherical Quadric Error Metric (SQEM). We address several long-standing robustness issues in dual-contouring and mesh extraction, including out-of-cell solutions, unstable feature classification, and redundant topological connections. To this end, we introduce virtual nodes, a feature-downgrading strategy, and a geometry-driven topology-aware cleanup procedure, enabling robust SQEM-based medial dual contouring with clean mesh outputs. Unlike prior point-cloud-based methods that produce either only 1D skeletal structures or incomplete medial features, our method preserves sharp geometric features from the input and reconstructs a complete medial structure, including sheets, curves, seams, and junctions. Compared to restricted-power-diagram-based approaches, our algorithm can handle point clouds as input, without having a strong requirement on water-tightness or manifoldness.

title: Revisiting out-of-distribution detection in semantic difference space

Regional-scale field-level estimation and mapping of tillage practices in areas with crop diversity
abstract: The imperative for sustainable agriculture has led to the promotion of conservation tillage practices, which are critical for maintaining soil health and reducing negative environmental impacts. However, the ability to verify the adoption of these practices at a regional scale and with minimal costs remains a challenge, particularly in regions with diverse crop systems. This study presents a satellite-imagery-based random forest classifier that integrates crop class information and a customized importance weighting technique for field-level, regional-scale mapping of tillage practices in crop-diverse regions. We use eastern Washington State, U.S., with multiple grains, legumes, and canola as a case study. Using 577 field-level ground-truth data points across two counties, the tillage classifier achieved a median overall accuracy of 84%, representing a 15 percentage point improvement over the baseline median overall accuracy of 69%, driven by the inclusion of crop class and the application of importance weighting. Specific crop classes, including grains, legumes, and canola, showed accuracy improvements of 6, 42, and 13 percentage points, respectively. While the model showed promising results, limitations such as overprediction of no-tillage in non-grain crop classes were identified, pointing to the need for further refinement with additional data. The model was applied to map tillage practices across dryland fields in eastern Washington State for the years 2012, 2017, and 2022, and the predictions were generally congruent with the USDA Census of Agriculture county-level statistics. This research offers a scalable tool for the verification of conservation tillage practice adoption, supporting both regional and global monitoring efforts for sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Human–AI Divergence in Ego-Centric Action Recognition Under Spatial and Spatiotemporal Manipulations
abstract: Humans consistently outperform state-of-the-art AI models in action recognition, particularly in challenging real-world conditions involving low resolution, occlusion, and visual clutter.e those utilised by humans Understanding the sources of this performance gap is essential for developing more robust and human-aligned models. In this paper, we present a large-scale human AI comparative study of egocentric action recognition using human-defined Minimal Identifiable Recognition Crops (MIRCs), defined as the smallest spatial or spatiotemporal regions sufficient for reliable human recognition. We used our previously introduced, Epic-ReduAct, a systematically spatially reduced and temporally scrambled dataset derived from 36 EPIC-KITCHENS videos, spanning multiple spatial reduction levels and temporal conditions. Recognition performance is evaluated using over 3,000 human participants, Side4Video, and Qwen 3.5 9B models. Our analysis combines quantitative metrics, Average Reduction Rate and Recognition Gap, with qualitative analyses of spatial (high-, mid-, and low-level visual features) and spatiotemporal factors, including a categorisation of actions into Low Temporal Actions (LTA) and High Temporal Actions (HTA). Results show that human performance exhibits sharp declines when transitioning from MIRCs to sub-MIRCs, reflecting a strong reliance on sparse, semantically critical cues such as hand object interactions. In contrast, the model degrades more gradually and often relies on contextual and mid- to low-level features, sometimes even exhibiting increased confidence under spatial reduction. Temporally, humans remain robust to scrambling when key spatial cues are preserved, whereas the model often shows insensitivity to temporal disruption, revealing class-dependent temporal sensitivities. Overall, our findings demonstrate that strong benchmark performance can obscure fundamental human AI misalignment and highlight limitations in current spatial and spatiotemporal representations, suggesting concrete directions for more efficient and human-aligned action recognition systems.

title: GRAIL: Granularity Adaptive Representation for Class-Incremental Learning with Granular-Ball
APEX: Exploiting Anatomical and Pathological Insights for Context-Aware Gaze Estimation
Disentanglement-Guided Multi-Teacher Relational Distillation for Federated Class-Incremental Facial Expression Recognition
abstract: Conventional facial expression recognition (FER) methods often train the model on large-scale centralized expression data. However, expression data are often distributed across heterogeneous devices and incrementally collected in practice. In this paper, we study a little-studied yet important task named federated class-incremental FER (FCI-FER), which aims to incrementally identify unseen compound expressions with the model initially trained on easily accessible basic expressions under the federated learning settings. To address the unique problems of catastrophic forgetting and heterogeneous disturbances across clients in FCI-FER, we propose a disentanglement-guided multi-teacher relational distillation (DMT-RD) method which follows a novel "distillation and disentanglement" paradigm. For local training, we design a multi-teacher hypergraph relational distillation (MTD) module to capture semantic relations between expressions and learn expression features. Meanwhile, we develop a disturbance encoding (DE) module to learn client-specific disturbance information. By minimizing the mutual information (MI) loss between the outputs of the MTD and DE modules, we can achieve feature disentanglement and reduce the negative influence of specific disturbances on local training. For global training, we introduce a multi-teacher learning strategy by clustering historical clients to comprehensively capture client diversity across communication rounds. Our method can effectively preserve old knowledge while learning new compound expressions under federated settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method against several state-of-the-art federated class-incremental learning methods on benchmark datasets.

title: FuseSR+: Spatial-Temporal Fusion for High-Scale Super-Resolution
abstract: The workload of real-time rendering is steeply increasing as the demand for high resolution, high refresh rates, and high realism rises, overwhelming most graphics cards. To mitigate this problem, one of the most popular solutions is to render images at a lower resolution to reduce rendering overhead and then manage to accurately upsample the low-resolution (LR) rendered image to the high-resolution (HR) results, a.k.a. super-resolution techniques. Theoretically, reconstructing a higher-resolution image requires integrating additional information beyond the rendered low-resolution image. Most existing methods predominantly rely on temporal information from low-resolution sources, such as historical frames. However, the temporal information accumulated frame-by-frame is generally too sparse to recover the fine details for high-scale super-resolution. To break the limit, this paper proposes an efficient and effective neural super-resolution method that utilizes non-aligned spatial and temporal information to achieve stable large-scale super-resolution. We introduce low-cost historical and current high-resolution auxiliary G-buffers as additional cues to enhance high-frequency detail reconstruction, spatial coherence, and temporal stability. To efficiently align and fuse various features — including spatial and temporal, low- and high-resolution features — under runtime constraints, we propose several novel technical modules, specifically, an H-Net architecture, a corresponding pixel shuffling and unshuffling layers for aligning low- and high-resolution features in a compact network, and a lightweight temporal feature recurrent module for aggregating HR temporal features. These techniques significantly reduce rendering overhead without noticeable quality deterioration. Experiments demonstrate that our method is able to produce temporally consistent reconstructions in both 4 × 4 and the more challenging 8 × 8 large-scale upsampling tasks at 4K resolution with real-time performance, while delivering substantially improved visual quality, significant performance gains, and remarkable temporal stability compared to existing methods.

title: Satellite embedding‑based mapping of grassland mowing frequency and its response to drought in Denmark
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Mowing frequency is a primary indicator of grassland management intensity, forage productivity, and biogeochemical dynamics. Yet, despite a growing body of literature, operational frameworks capable of mapping cutting regimes at a regional scale remain computationally demanding and lack independent benchmarking. Here, we evaluate the potential of Google AlphaEarth annual satellite embeddings to map grassland mowing frequency across Denmark (2017–2023) at 10-m resolution. Using farmer logs across multiple years (n = 346), Random Forest emerged as the top-performing classifier, achieving an overall accuracy of 0.73 and a macro F1-score of 0.65. Our workflow substantially outperformed the operational Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) Grassland Mowing Events (GRAME) benchmark (overall accuracy of 0.24). Latent embedding dimensions strongly correlated with macro-climatic and vegetation drivers (|ρ| > 0.8). Once deployed across the full nation extent, under 6 min of computing time, the model predictions proved ecologically consistent across pedological and agronomic gradients. We further applied Dirichlet regression to quantify how hydrological drought, indexed by a 6-month scale Standardised Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI-6), affects national mowing patterns. The extreme 2018 drought triggered a landscape-wide management de-intensification, shifting the intensive (≥4 cuts) regime into a 2 cuts system. During moderate droughts, regional responses diverged sharply: western regions exhibited agronomic resilience, whereas drier eastern islands repeatedly reverted to lower-intensity management. These results demonstrate that satellite foundation models can underpin scalable, automated agronomic monitoring and reveal grassland management’s acute sensitivity to drought, insights essential for adaptive land-use planning and national-scale environmental reporting.

title: Mapping small water bodies and their dynamics with deep learning: fusion of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery at semi-monthly 10 m spatial resolution
abstract: Mapping small water body (SWB) dynamics at high spatiotemporal resolution remains challenging because optical imagery is frequently obscured by clouds, whereas SAR imagery is affected by speckle noise and blurred boundaries. Existing Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion methods often have limited capability in fully exploiting the complementary information of the two sensors, leading to uncertainties in SWB mapping. Here we propose a deep learning-based method, the multiscale global-local water feature fusion network (MGLWNet), to map semi-monthly SWB dynamics via deep fusion of time-series Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery. A large-scale dataset containing 1,193,347 SWBs (<10 ha) was constructed. MGLWNet incorporates a cloud detection branch to improve feature discrimination under cloud-contaminated conditions and a multiscale global-local feature module that combines atrous spatial pyramid pooling and multi-scale self-attention to capture both fine spatial details and global contextual information. When tested on cloud-free and cloud-contaminated datasets, MGLWNet outperformed Random Forest and several state-of-the-art deep learning models. Compared with Sentinel-1-based surface water mapping, the proposed fusion strategy substantially reduced commission errors, while the cloud detection branch effectively decreased omission errors in cloudy regions. MGLWNet was applied to map semi-monthly 10 m surface water dynamics in high-density SWB areas of Hubei Province (185,900 km2) over the period 2017–2024. Unbiased accuracy estimates were performed for validation. The semi-monthly surface water maps have a producer's accuracy of 87.65% (±2.50%) and user's accuracy of 93.11% (±2.62%), respectively, with a 95% confidence interval. Compared with Landsat-based products, the method captured more frequent intra-monthly SWB variations and detected more long-term changes (e.g. the appearance and disappearance of small ponds). The resulting high-temporal-resolution dataset further enabled characterization of multiple SWB change types, including stable seasonal water, water gain, water loss, dry periods, and wet periods. This study highlights the importance of deep learning and image fusion for characterizing spatiotemporal continuous SWB dynamics.

title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

title: Bridging the Thermal Gap: Data-Model Collaborative Transfer for Infrared Perception
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Infrared visual perception fundamentally differs from visible-domain vision due to its distinct thermal imaging mechanism and varying imaging conditions. Existing methods typically decouple data construction from model transfer, overlooking their interdependence: model accuracy and robustness depend critically on the coverage and composition of training observations, while effective model transfer requires explicit modeling of infrared-specific imaging characteristics. To address this issue, we propose a data-model collaborative transfer framework for infrared visual perception. At the data level, a task-responsive generator learns weights over a feasible infrared imaging-variation space to construct informative training observations. At the model level, a formation-guided representation module derives complementary radiance-structure and response-detail descriptors from infrared observations. We further design a thermal-aware adapter that uses these descriptors to modulate intermediate representations and produce lightweight residual corrections for model transfer. A single-loop training strategy coordinates data generation, representation learning, and adapter optimization without expensive nested optimization. Extensive experiments on image enhancement, depth estimation, small-target detection, and semantic segmentation demonstrate consistent performance improvements across multiple foundation-model backbones with a small trainable parameter budget.

title: Real-World Spectral Compressive Imaging by Learning a Physics-Informed Forward Model
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Coded aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI) enables snapshot acquisition of hyperspectral image (HSI) by compressing a three-dimensional spectral data into a single two-dimensional measurement. While recent learning-based reconstruction methods achieve impressive performance on simulated datasets, their performance often degrades significantly on real CASSI systems, revealing a simulation-to-reality gap. This gap arises from a mismatch between the complex real imaging process and the reconstruction mappings learned from idealized simulated data. To bridge this simulation-to-reality gap, we propose a learnable physics-informed forward model (LPFM) that incorporates the physical structure of CASSI into a learnable proxy network to model the complex real imaging process. To train the LPFM, we construct the first real-world spectral compressive imaging (rSCI) dataset. The rSCI dataset contains 219 pairs of static HSI-CASSI images across diverse indoor and outdoor scenes, as well as additional dynamic CASSI videos. Leveraging rSCI and LPFM, we establish the first real-world benchmark for CASSI reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that incorporating data generated by LPFM effectively reduces the simulation-to-reality gap and consistently improves reconstruction performance across various state-of-the-art methods.

title: Knowledge-enhanced Incomplete Multi-view Clustering on Relational Knowledge
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC) methods have drawn increasingly attention these years, as their better potential to the complex real-world scenario. The key of the models in such tasks is how to perform high-quality imputation. Traditional intra-view and inter-view imputation strategies rely mainly on observed features. Such strategies may introduce semantic noise and biased estimations, making it difficult to recover the true semantics of missing views. Meanwhile, they are hard to directly apply to relational knowledge MVC, as fail to utilize the knowledge sufficiently. To this end, we propose a simple yet effective knowledge-enhanced anchor-based IMVC framework with two specific knowledge enhancement mechanisms, i.e., one for anchors, and the other for anchor graph. With the structural knowledge enhancement, the model can be gifted with better expressive ability and get good results. Extensive experiments compared with 10 models have proven the promising capacity of our method from 5 aspects, i.e., superiority, stability, sensitivity, complexity, and visualization. Notably, as the first work on IMVC on relational knowledge, 45 incomplete multi-view datasets are constructed with missing ratios ranging from 10% to 90%, which also facilitate the future research.

title: FLAME: Flow Guidance and Adaptive Frequency Fusion for All-in-One Mamba-Enhanced Video Restoration
abstract: All-in-One video restoration under adverse weather conditions (e.g., rain, snow, haze) remains challenging, as existing methods either rely on explicit optical flow alignment that becomes unreliable under heavy degradations, or employ implicit sequence modeling that lacks fine-grained temporal correspondence. We propose FLAME, a unified FLow guidance and Adaptive frequency fusion for all-in-one Mamba-Enhanced video restoration framework that synergistically combines explicit alignment with implicit modeling through three core components: (i) Dual-Path Mamba Modeling with complementary Space-Time Sequence Mamba and Hilbert-Sequence Mamba blocks for efficient spatiotemporal modeling with linear-complexity Mamba scanning; (ii) Flow-guided Lightweight Attention featuring degradation-aware flow estimation with triple quality assessment and temporal-spatial attention deformable fusion; (iii) Adaptive Frequency Residual Fusion employing learnable frequency decomposition and cross-channel attention for degradation-specific spectral enhancement. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: 35.50 dB PSNR on VRDS (+3.46 dB over RainMamba), 40.17 dB on LWDDS (+2.96 dB over RainMamba), 31.04 dB on W3 multiweather benchmark (+0.59 dB over AIM-VR), and 29.00 dB on RainSynAll100 rain-haze mixture (+1.33 dB over BasicVSR++), validating the effectiveness of explicit-implicit synergy for diverse weather degradation restoration.

title: BRepDSN: A Dual-stream Network Design for B-Rep Representation Learning Leveraging the Duality of Face and Boundary Vertices
abstract: Designing a neural network for Boundary Representation (B-Rep) models impacts fundamental tasks in Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Engineering (CAE), and Manufacturing (CAM). Existing methods primarily leverage face adjacency for B-Rep feature encoding, overlooking crucial boundary features from the B-Rep vertices. To address this, we introduce a novel dual-stream neural network, called BRepDSN, that explicitly leverages complementary features from both a Face-adjacency Graph (FG) and a Vertex-adjacency Graph (VG). Our method employs alternating message passing between these two graph streams with bidirectional information exchange. Specifically, faces gather boundary-aware cues from incident vertices through a dual mapping, while vertices are refined by face-level context, ensuring boundary-aware and semantically aligned feature encoding. To further boost the performance, we propose a face-vertex contrastive objective. This objective constructs contrastive pairs based on the duality between a face’s embedding and the aggregated embedding of its boundary vertices. Additionally, for segmentation tasks, we use an auxiliary classification loss to determine boundary edges, which acts as a dual task to the main face segmentation. BRepDSN can be used for multiple B-Rep processing tasks. We evaluate the following example tasks: 1) B-Rep Modeling Operation Segmentation, 2) Operation Step Segmentation, 3) B-Rep Classification, 4) Machining Feature Segmentation, and 5) Assembly Mating. Extensive experiments show that our method sets a new state of the art on all five tasks. For example, our method outperforms competing methods on the B-Rep modeling operation segmentation of CC3D (+14.65% mIoU), B-Rep classification of TMCAD (+4.9% oAcc), and the mating task of AutoMate [18] (+23.6% location acc, +21.0% type acc). The code for this paper are available on: https://github.com/shinodashx/BrepDSN.

title: Individual tree segmentation from terrestrial LiDAR: Benchmarking and forest structural analysis
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Individual tree segmentation from terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) is fundamental to automated forest inventory, yet recent benchmarks have reached divergent conclusions about method performance. We evaluated six methods on TreeScanPL10K, a dataset of 10,417 manually segmented trees across 272 plots of diverse Central European forest. Two are algorithmic (treeX, RayExtract) and four are deep learning (TreeLearn, TreeAIBox, SegmentAnyTree, ForestFormer3D). Beyond aggregate accuracy, we characterized the per-method failure modes and the forest structural attributes that drive performance variation. A clear hierarchy emerged: ForestFormer3D achieved the highest mean IoU (0.76), followed by the other deep-learning methods (0.67–0.71) and the algorithmic approaches (0.60–0.62). Coniferous species were segmented more accurately than broadleaves (0.70 vs. 0.64), with the widest gap for the deep-learning methods. Higher accuracy came at substantial computational cost: 15 min/plot for ForestFormer3D versus under a minute for the fastest methods. To identify what makes a plot difficult to segment, we ran two complementary analyses: one on field-inventory attributes, the other on crown-geometry descriptors derived from the reference annotations. The dominant signal came from crown geometry: the plot-level Mean Crown Area Index (Mean CAI), which summarizes how many crown layers stack vertically above each ground cell, was the strongest single correlate and the top-ranked feature for every method individually. Multi-layered canopies are the hardest to segment. The field-inventory pool added a related but distinct dimension: structural diversity in species composition and spatial arrangement contributed beyond the vertical-layering signal. All six methods degraded in parallel along these gradients, indicating that the evaluated methods share common difficulties in structurally complex stands. We release the exact 2 cm benchmark point clouds, plot-level attributes and results, point-level predictions from all six methods for 18 selected plots, and the evaluation code.

title: How should rural residential land in metropolitan suburbs be governed in the future? Evidence from Beijing using RGB-encoded multidimensional drivers and CNN prediction
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Rural residential land in metropolitan suburbs often expands, stabilizes and contracts within the same region, making static zoning inadequate for anticipatory governance. Existing land-use prediction approaches commonly use attribute vectors or remotely sensed image features, limiting their ability to reduce input dimensionality while preserving the spatial structure and combined effects of locational, accessibility and planning-related drivers. This study converts abstract geospatial drivers into red–green–blue (RGB) images and integrates them with convolutional neural network (CNN) models and ensemble prediction. Using suburban Beijing as a case, we evaluated 78 three-driver configurations across five deep-learning architectures, yielding 390 models. The modified VGG16 model achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.749. The optimal configuration combined village size, distance to the city center and expressway accessibility, indicating that rural residential land change is mainly associated with local development inertia, metropolitan gradients and external connectivity. A model using all nine drivers as nine-band input achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.758, compared with 0.749 for the three-driver RGB model; the latter used substantially fewer drivers while retaining higher precision and clearer variable semantics. Under the 2035 planning scenario, 36.57% of valid grids were predicted to increase, 33.90% to remain unchanged, 0.26% to decrease, and 29.27% were identified as uncertainty areas. These areas require flexible planning, dynamic monitoring and the avoidance of premature rigid decisions. By linking Earth Observation-derived land-change data with spatially structured driver representations, the workflow supports the explanation and prediction of land-use transitions and more adaptive governance of metropolitan suburbs.

title: A spatially and temporally comparable Remote Sensing Ecological Index via de-gradient national PCA for China’s resource-based cities
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Tracking the ecological quality of many cities over many years needs a Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) that stays comparable across space and time, yet standard constructions do not deliver one. A single national principal component analysis (PCA) is dominated by the between-city climate gradient, which loads heat and wetness with the wrong sign and inverts the index. We build a de-gradient national PCA (de-gradient PCA) whose weights come from the within-city component covariance under a fixed global normalization. The resulting index recovers the expected component signs where the single national PCA inverts them. It agrees with MODIS net primary productivity, an external ecological reference (city-mean r = 0.59 ), even after controlling for greenness (partial r = 0.50 ), and its weights are stable to city resampling and to leaving out any representative year. Applied to all 125 prefecture-level resource-based cities of China over 2003–2023, mean RSEI rose from 0.61 to 0.65 ( p < 1 0 − 4 ), with 83% of cities on a rising trend, faster than in 245 non-resource cities. Resource type set the ecological level more than development stage, and 13 cities in the arid northwest and coal belt stayed near 0.30. A spatial Durbin model identifies built-up land as the strongest local pressure and industrial structure as a persistent negative regional spillover; random-forest importance corroborates the built-up ranking.

title: SGDiff-OS: a semantic-guided diffusion model for SAR oil spill scattering and mask field generation
abstract: Marine oil spill remote sensing relies heavily on high-quality annotated data, yet the limited availability of well-annotated SAR oil spill samples with backscatter information and structural labels remains a challenge. To address the lack of structural consistency and scattering representation of existing generation methods, this study proposes a Semantic-Guided Diffusion for SAR Oil Spill Generation model (SGDiff-OS) for the joint generation of SAR oil spill backscatter coefficient σ° and corresponding binary oil spill labels, trained on a self-constructed SAR oil spill dataset. The model adopts a dual-channel conditional diffusion framework and incorporates semantic modulation to encode prior knowledge of spotted, blocky and slender morphologies, thereby improving structural representation and category controllability. Experimental results demonstrate that the generated samples show general agreement with real data in visual quality and overall statistical trends, although measurable distributional differences remain. The global mean σ° differs by approximately 1.96 dB between the real and generated samples. The generated samples retain the lower-backscatter relationship of oil-covered regions relative to seawater, although the oil-water contrast decreases from 6.59 dB to 4.65 dB. Furthermore, in an expert annotation evaluation of generated image mask pairs, the generated masks achieve an mIoU of 0.7658 and an F1-score of 0.8637 when evaluated against reference annotations. Under limited training data conditions, incorporating generated samples leads to a maximum improvement of 24.2% in mIoU, suggesting its potential value for sample augmentation under limited training conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed model can generate SAR oil spill samples with the dominant scattering trends of real SAR data, providing supplementary data for oil spill detection and segmentation tasks.

title: A rapid and robust scheme for CFOSAT SWIM nadir SWH retrieval
abstract: The Surface Waves Investigation and Monitoring (SWIM) onboard the China-France Oceanography Satellite (CFOSAT) has acquired unprecedented global ocean wave direction spectrum information. Additionally, it incorporates a nadir observation mode for significant wave height (SWH) based on principles analogous to conventional altimeters, which serves to calibrate the total energy of the wave spectrum. The retrieval of SWH from such nadir radar observations generally employs theoretical models to retrack the waveforms reflected by the sea surface, a method that demonstrates high accuracy in the open ocean environment. However, obtaining SWH using traditional retracking algorithms is computationally expensive. Furthermore, in coastal regions, waveforms are affected by factors such as the presence of land and sea ice, which means that the SWH retrieval relying on theoretical models often either fails or yields substantial errors. Leveraging the fact that SWIM does not necessitate precise ranging, we bypassed the decades-old retracking paradigm by developing dual neural network inversion models. These models perform direct SWH estimation following an initial classification of SWIM nadir waveforms. The first model targets standard open-sea waveforms, while the second is designed for coastal and sea-ice 'ocean-like' waveforms that deviate from normal patterns yet retain essential wave information. The results show that the normal-ocean model achieves a processing speed over 13 times faster than the MLE4 algorithm and nearly 22 times faster than the adaptive retracking algorithm, while maintaining comparable accuracy (RMSE = 0.31 m) to the SWIM nadir SWH product. Meanwhile, the ocean-like model enhances both the quantity and quality of usable SWH data in non-open ocean areas, leveraging the accurate mapping relationships established by the neural networks. Generally, a rapid and robust scheme was developed in this paper for retrieving nadir SWH from CFOSAT SWIM, providing an alternative methodology for retrieving nadir geophysical parameters in future nadir-looking radar systems.

title: A Neuro-symbolic Framework under Statistical Relational Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Neuro-symbolic systems aim to combine neural learning with symbolic reasoning for building interpretable and generalizable intelligent systems. While recent studies have explored different strategies for neuro-symbolic integration, existing approaches remain limited by (i) the absence of unified learning mechanisms between continuous neural representations and discrete symbolic concepts, (ii) weak interaction between neural prediction and symbolic reasoning, and (iii) restricted reuse of learned concepts for unseen reasoning scenarios. To address these issues, we propose NSF-SRL, a general neuro-symbolic framework based on statistical relational learning. NSF-SRL jointly models neural predictions, latent predicates and first-order logic rules within a unified probabilistic framework. For concept learning, NSF-SRL introduces a neuralized variational inference mechanism that learns predicate-level representations from neural representations and enables efficient neuro-symbolic interaction through variational expectation-maximization optimization. For concept manipulation, NSF-SRL allows learned concepts to be reused and composed with logic rules for interpretable explanation and compositional reasoning. Extensive experiments on digit image addition, zero-shot image classification and visual relationship detection, together with comprehensive analyses, demonstrate the effectiveness, generalization and scalability of NSF-SRL.

title: LLM-Enhanced 3D Generation: A Survey
Multi-View Synergistic Learning with Vision-Language Adaptation for Low-Resource Biomedical Image Classification
abstract: Accurate biomedical image classification under limited supervision remains challenging due to scarce annotations, subtle inter-class differences, and complex disease semantics. Pretrained vision-language models offer a promising foundation for alleviating data scarcity through knowledge transfer, yet effectively adapting them to low-resource biomedical tasks remains nontrivial. To this end, we propose Multi-View Synergistic Learning (MVSL), a unified framework that jointly considers three complementary perspectives: adaptation paradigms, representation granularity, and disease semantic relationships. Specifically, MVSL adopts tailored adaptation strategies for visual and textual encoders, accommodating their distinct representational characteristics while preserving pretrained knowledge. To capture both holistic image semantics and localized pathological evidence, we introduce multi-granularity contrastive learning that aligns global image representations and local visual features with disease-specific textual embeddings. Furthermore, we develop a Disease Semantic Graph (DSG) that leverages disease descriptions generated by large language models to model class-level semantic relationships and regularize adapted textual representations, thereby complementing discriminative learning and helping mitigate excessive specialization toward observed categories. Through the synergy of these complementary perspectives, MVSL enhances fine-grained discrimination while supporting semantic consistency and generalization to unseen categories. Extensive experiments on 11 public biomedical datasets spanning 9 imaging modalities and 10 anatomical regions demonstrate the effectiveness of MVSL in few-shot classification and base-to-novel generalization. The implementation and detailed experimental results are publicly available at https://github.com/luoxiaoliu/MVSL.

title: Invertible Gamut Mapping
abstract: Gamut mapping is a crucial component of the image signal processing (ISP) pipeline and color conversion between devices. Improper gamut mapping can introduce noticeable hue shifts and artifacts, resulting in poor visual quality. Although recent studies have significantly improved the fidelity of gamut extension through learning-based models and efficient metadata encoding schemes, the quality of gamut reduction and the intrinsic relationship between gamut reduction and extension have been largely overlooked. In this paper, we focus on developing deep learning-based approaches for gamut mapping that produce images with high color fidelity and perceptual quality for bidirectional conversion between wide gamut and small gamut. We propose an invertible framework that performs both gamut reduction and gamut extension within a single model. In the forward pass, the input wide-gamut image is decomposed into a clipped component and a residual component, which are jointly transformed into a small-gamut image and a latent variable. In the reverse pass, the small-gamut image and a Gaussian latent variable are used to reconstruct the wide-gamut image. To ensure that gamut reduction preserves hue and perceptual color similarity to the wide-gamut image, we introduce a self-supervised hue loss. We conduct experiments on three different gamut mapping scenarios: ProPhoto RGB to sRGB, BT.2020 to sRGB, and sRGB to a smaller "Toy" gamut. The proposed method outperforms previous metadata-free approaches in both color fidelity and perceptual quality across the evaluated gamut mapping scenarios.

title: TAETrack++: Trajectory Age Extension and Motion Refinement for Robust Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) is a vital task in computer vision, involving the continuous tracking and stable identification (ID) of multiple objects across video sequences. Existing methods often focus heavily on identity matching during association, neglecting the quality of trajectories, which affects object tracking performance. This article proposes a trajectory-age optimization approach for MOT that effectively improves its performance. First, we proposed TAE and TG to adaptively extend trajectory lifespans through IoU constraints and position awareness, allowing long-lost objects to be re-associated with their original trajectories instead of being initialized as new tracks, while suppressing erroneous matches. Second, by incorporating the track loss duration, our method enhances the observation-centric re-update mechanism and an adaptive Kalman filter with a dynamic noise scale, thereby reducing ID switches. Finally, our method combines Gaussian process-based interpolation with wavelet-thresholding denoising, leveraging the optimization of global smoothing and local denoising to improve trajectory smoothness and authenticity. Extensive experiments on the MOT17, MOT20, and DanceTrack standard datasets demonstrate that our method is competitive with the current state-of-the-art trackers and offers more robust ID maintenance across various challenging tracking scenarios.

title: Task Interference Mitigation via Confidence-Stratified Classifier Calibration for Prompt-based Continual Learning
abstract: Prompt-based continual learning is a promising direction that effectively leverages the capabilities of pre-trained models. These methods typically learn task-specific prompts and predict task identity to select the prompt during inference. However, task interference caused by prompt misselection significantly constrains their performance. Although several studies have attempted to mitigate this issue, they treat all samples equally, without specifically addressing the samples that are primarily affected by prompt misselection. In this paper, we stratify samples into three distinct categories according to their different responses to prompt misselection, including susceptible samples, refractory samples, and resilient samples. This stratification reveals that misselection-induced interference primarily manifests in susceptible samples, as only their classification correctness is influenced by prompt misselection, while other samples remain unaffected. This realization drives us to design a novel prompt-based approach called Confidence-Stratified Classifier Calibration (CoSC), which harnesses the complementary roles of all categories to safeguard susceptible samples. Specifically, we apply targeted optimization based on the unique properties of each category to cooperatively calibrate classifiers of both the prompt instruction part and the prompt selector, thereby protecting susceptible samples from dual perspectives. Extensive experiments show that CoSC achieves state-of-the-art performance across various benchmarks in class-incremental learning.

title: Fast and Compressed ADA-UNet: Refractive-Index Reconstruction with Latent-Domain Low-Rank Compression
abstract: Optical diffraction tomography (ODT) provides label-free three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) maps, but conventional reconstructions are highly sensitive to speckle noise and severely under-sampled illumination angles. We propose ADA-UNet, a compact two-stage framework in which (i) a modality-specific autoencoder learns a compact representation of stitched diffraction inputs, and (ii) a latent-domain ResUNet maps these interferometric latent codes to RI latent codes for non-iterative reconstruction. For compactness, the interferometry-to-RI mapping is expressed in Dirac form, but the network itself is implemented entirely with standard convolutional operators on GPU hardware. To reduce computational cost without changing the reconstruction objective, low-rank factorization is applied specifically to the ADA-aligned latent mapper. The resulting compressed model, ADA-UNetc, reduces the parameter count from 12.5M to 6.0M (a 52% reduction) while maintaining nearly unchanged reconstruction quality, with SSIM changing from 0.943 to 0.940 and NRMSE from 0.051 to 0.052. Across all evaluated ODT, cross-modal image-synthesis, and adaptation baselines, the proposed model achieves the best overall fidelity and a measured per-volume inference time of 187 s, compared with 221-840 s for the baselines. Experiments on synthetic and real 2-D/3-D data further demonstrate robustness under evaluation-time noise perturbations and sparse-angle acquisition, highlighting the potential of ADA-UNet for efficient and reliable quantitative phase imaging.

Toward a global snow water equivalent observing strategy
abstract: Current snow observations do not meet the data requirements established by the 2017 Decadal Survey and the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS) for global snow water equivalent (SWE) measurements. This paper evaluates existing spaceborne assets for global SWE and snow depth monitoring and identifies critical observational gaps that necessitate a dedicated snow observing strategy. We review snow data requirements across multiple application areas, including water resources, climate monitoring, weather forecasting, and disaster management, demonstrating the need for SWE measurements at 100 m to 4 km spatial resolution with 1- to 5-day temporal frequency and 10–20% accuracy. Analysis of current capabilities from missions including AMSR2, Sentinel-1, NISAR, and ICESat-2 reveals that while these sensors provide valuable SWE and depth information, they cannot, even when combined, deliver the comprehensive, high-resolution SWE data required for operational and scientific applications, observing only 40–60% of the global snowpack on a daily to weekly basis. We propose a global snow observing strategy centered on a core radar-based snow mission that would serve as the reference standard for a constellation of complementary sensors. This approach, combined with existing observations, ancillary data, advanced data fusion techniques, and land surface models, would provide accurate and timely SWE data essential for water resource management, climate research, and hazard mitigation.
